goal: Make the packaged Immune-Brain contracts Host-neutral about tool identity: remove the stale freeze_artifacts instruction the Kernel already performs internally, replace Pi-only tool names with the obligation they stand for, and add a focused guard so no packaged contract can again name a tool that is absent from the invoking Host's surface.

acceptance.assertion: No packaged contract under plugins/immune-brain/dist/ instructs a Host to call a tool that does not exist on that Host: the freeze_artifacts step is removed from imm-loop.md because runtime/assurance/coordinator.ts already performs artifact freeze inside advance_assurance, and every remaining imm_kernel_canary / imm_loop_action reference in imm-loop.md, imm-planner.md, and imm-review-retro.md is restated as the Host-neutral obligation instead of a single Host's tool spelling. No Host gains or loses a tool.

A new focused contract test tests/packaged-contract-tool-surface.test.ts enumerates every tool identifier appearing in the packaged contracts and fails unless each one is registered on at least one Host tool surface (runtime/claude/mcp_server.ts for Claude Code, the Pi extension registration for Pi). The test fails against the pre-change contracts, which is the evidence that it catches the regression it names.

The doc pipeline stays consistent after the edits: the three files remain SKILL_OWNED_ENTRIES in scripts/dist-sync-manifest.ts, their minimal skills/*/SKILL.md loaders are unchanged, and the existing dist sync and skill consistency guards still pass.
